title: Logarithm routine meets its time bound
statement: Let $\mathrm{lim}$ be machine limits, $P$ a program, $d,p,x\in\mathbb N$, and $\mu:\mathbb N\to\mathbb Z$. Suppose procedure $p$ in $P$ is the routine that computes the base-two logarithm, and the word limit is at least $2x+2$. Then calling procedure $p$ at depth $d$ with the single argument $x$ and initial memory $\mu$ has an execution within time $14\lfloor\log_2 x\rfloor+12$ whose returned value is $\lfloor\log_2 x\rfloor$ and whose final memory is $\mu$.
hypotheses_covered: Procedure $p$ in $P$ is the specified logarithm routine
The word limit is at least $2x+2$
